column5: Case 01 — A service that records new customer entries.POST /customers — accepts a JSON body with an email-formatted field. Access to this endpoint is restricted by a role-based annotation on the controller class (a "user" role is required). The request body parameter is not annotated to trigger validation of the body's field constraints before the method runs.
column6: Case 02 — A service that lets a user regain access to their account.POST /api/recovery/request — accepts a JSON body containing an email address. Generates a new random identifier, stores it associated with the submitted email, and returns that identifier directly in the JSON response body. No other input or check is required.POST /api/recovery/complete — accepts a JSON body containing an identifier and a new credential value. If the identifier matches one generated by the /request endpoint, the request succeeds; otherwise it is rejected. No other check is performed.
column7: Case 03 — A service that manages shipping labels for orders.POST /api/labels — accepts an order id and carrier name, generates a random tracking identifier, and stores the label. GET /api/labels/{tracking} — returns a label by its tracking identifier. POST /api/labels/{tracking}/void — marks a label with the given tracking identifier as voided. None of the three methods requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
column8: Case 04 — A minimal service exposing a health check.GET /health — restricted by a role-based annotation (a "user" role is required); returns a fixed string. Separately, the project's configuration file (application.properties) contains the following as plain text: spring.datasource.username=service_user / spring.datasource.password=hunter2
column9: Case 05 — A service for uploading and retrieving files.POST /api/files — accepts a multipart file upload, stores its bytes and metadata in memory under a generated id. GET /api/files — returns metadata (id, name, size) for every stored file. GET /api/files/{id}/content — returns the raw bytes of a stored file by its id. None of the three methods requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
column10: Case 06 — A service for creating orders.POST /orders — restricted by a role-based annotation on the controller class (a "user" role is required). The request body parameter is annotated to trigger validation, and the request's order-id field is marked as required (must not be blank).
column11: Case 07 — A service that receives and stores webhook notifications from a payment provider.POST /webhooks/payments — accepts a raw request body and a header named X-Payment-Signature. Computes an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the request body using a secret value read from configuration, and only stores the event if the computed signature matches the supplied header value; otherwise responds with an unauthorized status. GET /webhooks/payments — returns every previously stored event body. No header, credential, or other check is performed before this method runs.
column12: Case 08 — A service that stores provider-issued payment method tokens (explicitly not raw card numbers) for customers.POST /internal/payment-methods — accepts a header named X-Payment-Vault-Key and a request body; the header value is compared against a value read from configuration, and the method only proceeds if they match. GET /internal/payment-methods/customer/{customerId} — accepts the same header; the same comparison is performed before returning the stored payment methods for the given customer id.
column13: Case 09 — A service handling a checkout/payment flow.POST /checkout — accepts a JSON body containing a reference value (required, must not be blank) and returns that same reference value. No header, credential, or other check is performed. Separately, the project contains a class with the following method, used for authenticating a submitted password against a stored one. It is not called from the endpoint above, or from anywhere else shown in the project: public boolean authenticate(String password, String submittedPassword) { return password == submittedPassword; }
column14: Case 10 — A service for issuing and revoking integration credentials.POST /internal/api-keys — accepts a header named X-Api-Key-Admin-Key, compared against a value read from configuration; only proceeds on a match. Generates a new random 32-byte value, stores only its SHA-256 hash, and returns the raw generated value once, in the response. DELETE /internal/api-keys/{id} — accepts the same header and comparison as above before removing a stored credential's hash by id.
column15: Case 11 — A service that issues and refreshes access tokens.POST /internal/refresh-tokens — accepts a header named X-OAuth-Internal-Key, compared against a value read from configuration; only proceeds on a match. Generates and returns a token pair. POST /oauth/token — accepts a header named X-OAuth-Client-Key and a request body containing a grant type and a refresh-token value. Proceeds only if the header matches a configured value and the grant type equals a fixed expected string; then looks up the supplied refresh-token value against previously issued ones, rejecting if not found. If found, issues a new token pair.
column16: Case 12 — A class providing password authentication. This project has no HTTP endpoints — it is a single utility class plus an application entry point.The entire contents of the class beyond the entry point: public boolean authenticate(String password, String submittedPassword) { return password == submittedPassword; }
column17: Case 13 — A service for submitting and moderating product reviews.POST /api/products/{productId}/reviews — accepts a star rating (1–5, validated) and text (required); creates a review. GET /api/products/{productId}/reviews — lists reviews for a product. DELETE /api/products/{productId}/reviews/{id} — removes a review by id. None of the three methods requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
column18: Case 14 — A minimal service exposing a route status check.GET /routes/status — no check required; returns a fixed string. Separately, the project's configuration file (application.properties) contains the following as plain text: gateway.upstream.apikey=sk-live-gw-9f8e7d
column19: Case 15 — A service managing an email mailing list and campaign sends.POST /api/newsletter/subscribe — accepts an email-formatted address, adds it to the subscriber list. POST /api/newsletter/unsubscribe — accepts an email-formatted address, removes it from the subscriber list. POST /api/newsletter/campaigns — accepts a request body, and returns the current subscriber count together with a status of "QUEUED". None of the three methods requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
column20: Case 16 — A service for creating and retrieving orders.POST /api/orders — creates an order from a validated request body (product code required, quantity must be positive). GET /api/orders/{id} — retrieves an order by id. A separate configuration class in the same project applies HTTP Basic authentication to every request reaching the application, with cross-site request forgery protection disabled.
column21: Case 17 — A service for generating and downloading business metric reports.POST /api/reports — accepts a request body, generates a report (containing fixed sample values for signups and revenue) under a generated id. GET /api/reports/{id}/download — downloads a previously generated report as a CSV file attachment, by id. Neither method requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
column22: Case 18 — A service simulating a third-party payment provider.POST /api/payments/charges — accepts a positive amount and a currency code (both required). Checks that a configured provider API key value is not blank before proceeding (rejects if it is); does not compare that value against anything supplied by the caller. Generates a random charge id and stores/returns the result. GET /api/payments/{id} — retrieves a stored charge by id. No check performed.
column23: Case 19 — A service for resetting a forgotten password.POST /api/password-resets — accepts an email-formatted address. Generates a new 32-byte random value, stores only a SHA-256 hash of it (associated with the email and a 15-minute expiry), and returns an empty response — the generated value itself is not included in the response body. POST /api/password-resets/confirm — accepts a token value and a new password value (both required). Looks up the hash of the supplied token; rejects if not found or if the associated expiry has passed.
column24: Case 20 — A service for recording stock-count adjustments.POST /api/inventory/{sku}/adjustments — accepts an integer delta (no minimum or maximum enforced) and a required reason string; records the adjustment. GET /api/inventory/{sku}/adjustments — lists the adjustment history for a SKU. Neither method requires any header, credential, or other check before running.
